title: Where a person's data enters, rests, and leaves
summary: Four ways in, five places it rests, four things derived from it, three ways it comes back out to the person, and five services that see a piece of it.
note: The claim this diagram is really making is that the list of exits is short and each one is nameable. Only two kinds of thing leave: a bundle the person asked for, and the minimum a third party needs to do its job. Three details worth pulling out. Records marked sensitive are excluded from an export unless the person opts in, and the exclusion is transitive: edges touching a sensitive record, and the revisions and atoms that describe it, go too, because a partial exclusion would leave the shape of what was hidden. The one outbound payload that is text a person wrote is the place query sent to an unauthenticated public geocoder. And the control-plane tables are deliberately outside the graph repository. Identities, memberships, lifecycle and provider events are operational records, not exportable career data, which is exactly what keeps them out of the export bundle. Nothing here models an analytics pipeline, a telemetry sink, a message queue or a model provider, because the repository contains none: there is no LLM call anywhere in the API, and the "Ask" surface is a deterministic ranking over the local graph.

zones.label: How it gets in
zones.note: Every one of these is input from outside the process, whether it was typed, uploaded, or fetched from a third party on the person's behalf.

zones.label: Where it rests
zones.note: One Postgres database and one secret store. Which table a record lands in decides whether it is exportable career data or operational record.

zones.label: What is computed from it
zones.note: All four are recomputable from the stored records. None is a source of truth, and losing any of them costs a rebuild, not data.

zones.label: What comes back to the person
zones.note: Bytes crossing back out of the system to the machine of the person who owns them.

zones.label: What a third party sees
zones.note: Five services. Note what none of them receives: no third party is ever sent the graph.

nodes.label: Capture line and record forms
nodes.note: The ⌘K capture line parses one typed line into a plan of linked records, previewable before commit and committed as one transaction; the structured forms cover every node type. Both land as ordinary graph writes with provenance and a revision.

nodes.label: Uploaded files
nodes.note: LinkedIn exports, vCard contacts, ICS calendars, browser bookmarks, a résumé to disassemble, and a Vitae graph bundle. Read client-side and posted as text, never multipart. Nothing reaches the graph until a person reviews the staged rows.

nodes.label: GitHub repository sync
nodes.note: The one import that bypasses staging: repositories become repository nodes and their languages become skill nodes with USES_SKILL edges, written directly and tagged `source_ref: 'github_sync'`. It creates no batch, so it cannot be rolled back the way a staged import can.

nodes.label: Place lookup
nodes.note: A person types a place; the result becomes coordinates and a display name on a place node. The query goes out before anything comes in, which is what makes this both an entrance and an exit.

nodes.label: Nodes, edges and revisions
nodes.note: The career graph, and the audit history of every durable mutation beside it. Deletion is a timestamp here, not a removal.

nodes.label: The other twenty-one document tables
nodes.note: Atoms and their variants and skills, targets, résumés, letters, templates, reminders, tags and taggings, attachments, merges, imports, saved views, habit checks and deduplication state. All twenty-four document tables carry the workspace as part of their primary key, not merely as a filter beside it.

nodes.label: Raw upload chunks
nodes.note: The original bytes of an import, kept only while the batch is open for review, and deleted at every exit: commit, discard, or rollback. The most sensitive artifact in the system is also the shortest-lived.

nodes.label: Control-plane tables
nodes.note: Users, workspaces, memberships, lifecycle states and events, billing customers, subscriptions and provider events. Kept outside the graph repository on purpose, which is what stops them appearing in an export.

nodes.label: Secret store
nodes.note: Never the database. An injected environment variable, or a git-ignored file store with restrictive permissions. A credential found in the old database location is migrated out and deleted on read, so a backup taken afterwards no longer carries a usable token.

nodes.label: Search index
nodes.note: In-memory, per workspace, rebuilt from live nodes when a mutation marks it dirty. Indexes titles, subtitles, notes and a whitelist of text-bearing properties.

nodes.label: Relationship signals
nodes.note: Contact strength, reconnect lanes, warm introduction paths and the who-to-call ranking, all deterministic functions over one graph read per request.

nodes.label: Duplicate candidates
nodes.note: A cached scored pairing of records that might be the same person or organisation. Invalidated explicitly by any write that could change the answer, rather than left to expire.

nodes.label: Résumé model and LaTeX
nodes.note: Selected evidence assembled into a résumé model, then rendered through a template into a LaTeX document. Every user-controlled string passes the escape layer here, before it can reach a compiler.

nodes.label: Export bundle
nodes.note: A streamed zip: JSONL for every durable collection with document identity preserved, an Obsidian-readable Markdown vault with one note per live node, the stored blobs, and a manifest with schema version, counts and SHA-256 checksums. It is the anti-lock-in guarantee, and apps/api/src/services/restore.ts:47 is the half that reads it back.

nodes.label: Saved view as CSV
nodes.note: A targeted extract beside the full bundle. Every cell that a spreadsheet would execute as a formula is prefixed first, and sensitive records are dropped unless explicitly requested.

nodes.label: Compiled PDF, or the LaTeX source
nodes.note: A compiled résumé, returned to the browser as a PDF. When the build service is unreachable the response says so and hands back the .tex instead, so the flow degrades rather than fails. Cover letters are in this path now. They go through the same signed call to the same sandboxed compiler, against templates/letter-classic, and degrade the same way: unreachable means the response says so and hands back the .tex, and the letter stays a draft rather than being recorded as finalized against a PDF that does not exist.

nodes.label: Firebase Auth
nodes.note: Sees the sign-in itself and the token it issued. What comes back into the system is three fields: a stable identifier, a verified email, and the provider that proved it.

nodes.label: Paddle
nodes.note: Receives an email address and two opaque identifiers as custom data; returns subscription events that never touch the graph, only the control plane. No career data is sent, and no entitlement is inferred from anything the browser reports.

nodes.label: Cloudinary
nodes.note: Holds compiled artifact bytes under a content hash namespaced by workspace, with a private delivery type reachable only through short-lived signed URLs. It is the only durable store of a person's data outside the database.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.note: Receives the personal access token and an ETag; returns the person's own repository list.

nodes.label: Nominatim
nodes.note: Receives the place text as typed, or a coordinate pair, with no credential and no account. The only third party that sees free text a person wrote.

links.label: Commit, in one transaction
links.carries: Nodes, edges and a revision per write

links.label: Records that are documents rather than graph nodes
links.carries: Atoms, reminders, targets, résumés, letters, saved views

links.label: Stage the original bytes
links.note: Held only for the life of the review.

links.label: Stage the parsed rows
links.carries: One reviewable row per record, each with a duplicate verdict

links.label: Commit the accepted rows
links.carries: Nodes, edges and atoms tagged with the batch identifier
links.note: That tag is what makes a per-batch rollback possible later.

links.label: Ask for the repository list
links.carries: The token from the secret store

links.label: Repositories and languages become records
links.carries: Repository nodes, skill nodes, USES_SKILL edges

links.label: Search or reverse-geocode
links.carries: The place text the person typed

links.label: The chosen hit becomes a place
links.carries: Coordinates, a display name and a country code

links.label: Enrolment persists the verified principal
links.carries: The identifier, the email and the provider

links.label: Verified webhooks are recorded and applied
links.carries: The event payload, the subscription status and the derived access state
links.note: The raw event is kept as evidence even when it names no known workspace.

links.label: One graph read, many derived answers
Select evidence against the page budget
links.carries: Atoms, their variants, the target's keywords and the template

links.label: Render, compile, return
links.carries: LaTeX out to the compiler, PDF bytes back

links.label: Finalising stores the artifact
links.carries: PDF bytes and their content hash

links.label: Stream every collection and a vault note per node
links.carries: JSONL with document identity preserved, plus Markdown
links.note: Sensitive records and everything transitively depending on them are excluded unless the person opts in.

links.label: Stored blobs are pulled back into the zip
links.carries: The bytes, keyed by content hash
links.note: So the bundle is complete on its own, not a set of references to a service.

links.label: A saved query, flattened to rows
links.carries: Identifier, type, title, subtitle, updated time, provenance

links.label: Never crosses
links.note: Stated as an absence, because it is a deliberate design choice rather than an omission: the control plane sits outside the graph repository so an export cannot reach it.
